                                                 ORDER


        This matter comes before the Court on pro se Plaintiffs (i) Motion for Entry of a

 Scheduling Order and, as necessary, an Initial Pretrial Conference and (ii) Motion for an Order

 Directing Completion of the Rule 26(1) Conference and Submission of a Discovery Plan. (Dkts.

 103, 105). Plaintiff seeks multiple forms of relief. First, Plaintiff requests entry of a scheduling

 order. Second, Plaintiff requests an order directing the parties to complete a Rule 26(f) conference

 and file respective discovery plans. Third, Plaintiff requests an initial pretrial conference. Fourth,

 if any of these steps are postponed. Plaintiff requests that the order state the date or event on which

 scheduling will next be addressed. In deference to Plaintiffs pro se status, the Court will liberally

 construe his filings. See Erickson v. Pardus, 551 U.S. 89 (2007). However, even applying this

 liberal standard. Plaintiff has not established that he is entitled to the relief he seeks.

        There are three pending motions to dismiss in this matter. The last of which was filed on

 September 2, 2026. See Dkts. 10, 21, & 45. “Given that Rule 16 Scheduling Orders initiate

 discovery obligations, it is standard for courts to wait until any preliminary motions such as

 motions to dismiss or to remand arc resolved to avoid expensive or otherwise burdensome


 discovery on potentially frivolous claims.” Giirri Rubio v. MiilUn, No. 25-CV-2756-ABA, 2026

 WI. 1194557, at *3 (D. Md. May 1, 2026). Here, the record reflects that the District Judge has

 chosen to refrain from beginning any discovery until resolution of the pending motions to dismiss.

 Accordingly, Plaintiffs Motions (Dkts. 103, 105) arc DKNIKl) without prejudice.

        ENTERED this 29lh day of October, 2026.
